CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization for fever, elevated white blood cell count, constipation, and blood pressure fluctuations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury who was admitted to District Regional Hospital from 06/29/2021 to 07/02/2021. She presented with increasing concerns for spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. In the emergency department, she was febrile with white blood cell count of 23,000. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. Concerns were raised for urinary tract infection and she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She has a supra-pubic catheter. Cultures were obtained. She gradually improved and was discharged after clinical improvement. Today she presents for follow-up. The patient believes her symptoms were primarily related to constipation and autonomic dysreflexia from her quadriplegia rather than a true urinary tract infection. She recalls not having regular bowel movements during hospitalization but experienced significant clinical improvement after a substantial bowel movement at home. She notes the hospitalization occurred during a particularly hot period in late June. Currently, she reports feeling back to her normal self and denies pain or discomfort.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Currently: Denies pain or discomfort anywhere. Reports feeling well and back to baseline.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury
- Dysreflexia
- Chronic constipation
- Recurrent urinary tract infection concerns (has supra-pubic catheter)

MEDICATIONS
- Miralax daily
- Lactulose as needed for severe constipation (reports it takes about 2 days to work)
- Vitamin C supplement
- Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient stays indoors more during hot weather but does go out occasionally. She is unvaccinated for COVID-19, expressing concerns about unknown long-term side effects and reported cases of "vaccine injury." She does not receive annual flu shots. She uses vitamin supplementation and employs some homeopathic approaches. She believes she is young and healthy enough to manage COVID infection despite her respiratory limitations.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Patient instructed to take deep breaths; breathing normal and adequate. General: Patient appears well and in no acute distress.

RESULTS
- White blood cell count elevated at 23,000 during hospitalization
- Urine cultures not impressive and not conclusive for urinary tract infection
- Abdominal X-rays performed during hospitalization
- CT scan not performed
- Patient's baseline WBC has been normal in prior years; currently slightly elevated

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Acute to Chronic Constipation: Patient's recent hospitalization was likely related more to significant constipation and dysreflexia from her quadriplegia rather than true UTI. Discussed possible role of dehydration during the hot weather period in June contributing to worsening constipation. Patient maintains adequate bowel regimen with daily Miralax and lactulose for breakthrough constipation. Plan to obtain fasting labs in 2-3 weeks including complete blood count to reassess white blood cell count and ensure it normalizes. Also will obtain lipid panel/cholesterol labs as patient is due for this screening. Two purposes will be accomplished with one visit. If white blood cell count remains elevated, this would suggest other bowel pathology that needs further investigation.

Quadriplegia: Stable. Continues to experience dysreflexia which can contribute to vital sign fluctuations and associated symptoms.

COVID-19 Vaccine Status: Patient currently unvaccinated. Had extensive discussion regarding vaccine safety and importance of vaccination. Physician counseled that patient is at high risk for severe COVID-19 given her quadriplegia and respiratory limitations. Emphasized that vaccination is the only truly effective preventative measure for COVID-19 and that vitamin supplementation alone is not adequate protection. Addressed patient's concerns about vaccine side effects, noting that serious adverse events are very rare and that the physician has seen significant morbidity and mortality from COVID-19 in practice. Reassured patient that vaccine is safe and that the physician has been vaccinated, as have his children. Patient remains hesitant but open-minded. Physician expressed concern but ultimately respects patient's autonomy in medical decision-making. Encouraged patient to reconsider and contact with any further questions.

Follow-up appointment in 2-3 weeks for lab work.
